new_entities.name: Off-label hyperbaric oxygen therapy
new_entities.description: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy promoted beyond established indications for neurological, recovery, cognitive, or post-viral syndromes.

new_entities.name: Various outcomes
new_entities.description: A broad mix of clinical outcomes across several off-label conditions rather than one validated indication.

edges.effect_quant: HBOT has positive evidence in some narrow disease states, but a 2024 living systematic review of long-COVID interventions found no compelling evidence for hyperbaric oxygen, while a 2023 safety meta-analysis showed adverse effects were more common with HBOT than control conditions.
edges.population: patients receiving hyperbaric oxygen outside core approved indications, especially for post-concussion symptoms, long COVID, wellness, or broad neurorecovery claims
edges.mechanism: Hyperoxia under pressure can alter tissue oxygen delivery, inflammatory signaling, and repair pathways, but biological plausibility does not guarantee broad clinical effectiveness across diverse off-label conditions.
edges.summary: Off-label HBOT is best treated as a contested umbrella claim rather than a single validated therapy. Some targeted conditions may show promise, but the overall off-label landscape remains heterogeneous, indication-specific, and often ahead of the evidence.
edges.caveats: Do not merge approved-indication evidence with wellness or off-label claims. Safety, cost, and condition-specific null results matter, especially where sham-controlled or living-review evidence remains unconvincing.

evidence.notes: Interventions for the management of long covid (post-covid condition): living systematic review.

evidence.citation: Zhang Y et al 2023 Front Med (Lausanne)
evidence.notes: Adverse effects of hyperbaric oxygen therapy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
